question: How do we check whether a shuttle has the right speed?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: the sources do not say how to check whether a shuttle has the right speed. Law 3.1 (sentences 1 and 2) gives the testing stroke — a full underhand stroke contacting the shuttle over the back boundary line, hit at an upward angle parallel to the side lines — and Law 3.2 (sentence 1) gives the pass criterion: a shuttle of correct speed lands not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line (Diagram B). Together these answer how the check is done. Related but not answering the 'how': ITTO 3.5.4.1 (who should test), 3.5.4.2 (test all speeds from both ends), 3.5.4.4 (assess strength of shot, trajectory, correct location), 3.6.3 (1) (Referee re-checks during play that the selected speed still appears correct), and ITTO 5.13.3 (1) (Referee is sole judge of shuttle speed).
answer.answer:
Under the Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, a shuttle is tested for speed by having a player use a full underhand stroke which makes contact with the shuttle over the back boundary line, hitting it at an upward angle and in a direction parallel to the side lines (Clause 3.1). The shuttle has the correct speed if it lands not less than 530 mm and not more than 990 mm short of the other back boundary line (Clause 3.2).
Related (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 3.5.4.1): "The shuttles should be tested by an active player in the tournament, preferably a male player, or a qualified person approved by the Referee."
Related (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 3.5.4.2): "All available speeds shall be tested from both ends of the court."
Related (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 3.5.4.4): "When assessing the result of the shuttle test, take into account the manner in which the shuttles were hit (strength of shot and trajectory), and whether they were hit from the correct location (over the back line) (Law 3)."
Related (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 3.6.3): "Shuttle Speed The Referee shall at all times, when observing play, consider whether the shuttle speed selected before play started still appears to be correct."
Related (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 5.13.3): "The Referee shall be the sole judge for deciding the speed of the shuttles to be used."
